An object is launched from a height of 130 feet above the ground. A quadratic function f models the height above the ground, in feet, of the object t seconds after it is launched. According to the model, 2 seconds after the object is launched, it reaches a maximum height of 194 feet above the ground. Which equation defines f?
verified: logical: vertex form with maximum (vertex) at t=2, height 194, standard -16t^2 gravity coefficient gives f(t)=-16(t-2)^2+194; f(0)=-16(4)+194=130 matches the given launch height, confirming D

problem: In triangle ABC, the measure of angle C is 90 degrees. The cosine of angle A is 60/61. What is the sine of angle B?
verified: logical: in a right triangle with the right angle at C, angles A and B are complementary, so sin B = cos A = 60/61

ax^2 + 176x + c. In the given expression, a and c are positive constants. If px + q is a factor of the expression, where p and q are positive constants, what is the greatest possible value of ac?
verified: sympy/AM-GM: if ax^2+176x+c=(px+q)(rx+s) with p,q,r,s>0, then a=pr, c=qs, 176=ps+qr; by AM-GM ps+qr>=2*sqrt(ps*qr)=2*sqrt(pr*qs)=2*sqrt(ac), so 176>=2*sqrt(ac) -> ac<=88^2=7744, with equality achievable when ps=qr=88
